extrapolation_assumption: Corpus sizes beyond the observed 1,396 hold the LOSS PROFILE fixed: the mean loss of the best c-fraction is read off the observed distribution and applied at the larger n. This answers 'what if there were more data like this', which is the question the write-up's sentence asks. It is NOT a prediction about any real larger corpus, and a corpus with a different loss profile has a different answer.
interpretation: The write-up said the corpus would need to be roughly 13x larger before the gap could close. That closes the RISK test only. The acceptance floor is tested on a Clopper-Pearson LOWER bound, and at exactly the floor coverage that bound approaches the floor from below and never reaches it at any n - so NO corpus of any size certifies at exactly 20% coverage, and a certificate requires coverage strictly above the floor. The smallest corpus admitting one, and the coverage it needs, are computed here over BOTH constraints jointly.

smallest_corpus_admitting_a_certificate._notice: A BAND, NOT A POINT, and the reason is the reason the cost figure is a band: the endpoints differ only by a modelling choice the data does not settle. Rounding the loss profile to a whole observed group and interpolating a fractional one are both defensible readings of 'the same profile at a larger n' and they disagree by about 1.5%. An independent reviewer's own derivation landed at 29,926 (21.4x), a third point in the same band. Publishing any single endpoint would present a modelling decision as a measurement, which is this project's recorded defect class.
smallest_corpus_admitting_a_certificate.what_is_robust: The ORDER of the answer, not its third significant figure: roughly 21x the observed corpus, and - unlike the withdrawn 13x - only at coverage STRICTLY ABOVE the floor. The structural fact needs no extrapolation at all and is exact: at exactly the floor coverage the acceptance lower bound is below the floor at every n.

witness_at_the_observed_corpus.note: The smallest prefix at the observed corpus that clears the ACCEPTANCE floor on its Clopper-Pearson lower bound. A witness for 'some model could certify here' must clear BOTH tests, so it must be stated at this k and this ceiling - not at the 20%-coverage prefix, which clears the risk test and fails acceptance at 0.16566.
